CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit for reassessment of anxiety management, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, reporting a modest improvement in his overall anxiety levels since the last visit. He states that the increase in sertraline dosage to 100 mg daily has contributed positively to his mood, particularly during work hours. However, he continues to experience significant sleep disturbances, with an average of only 4 to 5 hours of sleep per night, often interrupted by multiple awakenings. Mr. Smith describes persistent fatigue, which he attributes to both the poor quality of sleep and ongoing anxiety. He mentions that the tension-type headaches have persisted, occurring approximately four times a week, typically in the late afternoon, and are often triggered by stress at work.
Mr. Smith has been compliant with his medication regimen, including the recently prescribed cognitive behavioral therapy for insomnia (CBT-I), which he reports has been somewhat beneficial in improving his sleep hygiene. However, he expresses a desire for additional strategies to manage his headaches, which he describes as moderate in intensity and responsive to over-the-counter analgesics.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 100 mg daily 2. Melatonin 3 mg at bedtime 3. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 4. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer and reports a slight increase in physical activity, having started a walking routine three times a week. He maintains a sedentary lifestyle outside of work and continues to consume alcohol socially, with no changes in tobacco use. He expresses ongoing interest in stress management techniques and has begun practicing mindfulness meditation.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Reports reduced anxiety levels, ongoing sleep disturbances, no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms noted. - Neurological: Headaches as described, no visual changes or focal neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or shortness of breath. - General: Persistent fatigue, no fever or weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 70 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert and oriented, in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact, no motor or sensory deficits. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative, maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable with reduced anxiety.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline 100 mg daily; monitor for further improvement and consider referral to a psychiatrist for possible augmentation therapy if no significant progress is noted by the next visit. 2. Insomnia: Continue melatonin 3 mg at bedtime; continue CBT-I and encourage adherence to sleep hygiene practices. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue ibuprofen 400 mg as needed; consider referral to a pain management specialist if headaches persist or worsen. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Continue to encourage regular physical activity and mindfulness practices; discuss the potential benefits of a structured exercise program.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2026-12-01 to evaluate symptoms and treatment effectiveness. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any worsening of symptoms or side effects from medications.
